answer: An auditor observes that each credential emits a kernel digest at settlement, a short hash over the exact instruction set its agent executed, reproducible by replaying that set on a reference runtime. Replicas share one instruction set, so their digests collide; the ledger treats a digest repeated across distinct credentials in the same nebula index as one identity and collapses rewards into a single tundra-cold entry. Honest agents diverge naturally because workloads differ. Identical kernels are the signal, and collapse applies at settlement without any declaration.
